 {H-type foliation}

 {H-type foliation}


H-type foliations were introduced by Baudoin, Grong, Rizzi and Vega-Molino as a geometric framework extending several important classes of sub-Riemannian structures, including H-type groups, \(K\)-contact manifolds and \(3K\)-contact manifolds; see  {Bau2022Htype}.
 
Let
\((M,  H,g)\) be a totally geodesic Riemannian foliation with orthogonal splitting
\[
    TM=  H   V,
\]
and let \( \) be the associated Bott connection with torsion \(T\). For
\(Z   V\), define \(J_Z:  H   H\) by
\[
      J_ZX,Y 
    =
      Z,T(X,Y) ,
      X,Y   {X}_{  H}.
\]
The foliation is said to be of  {H-type}(or Heisenberg-type) if
\[
      J_ZX,J_ZY 
    =
    |Z|^2  X,Y ,
\]
or equivalently(by the skew-symmetry of $J_Z$),
\[
    J_Z^2=-|Z|^2 {Id}_{  H}.
\]
Thus each vertical direction induces, after normalization, an orthogonal complex structure on the horizontal bundle. In particular, the horizontal distribution is bracket generating of step two, and the maps \(J_Z\) encode quantitatively the non-integrability of \(  H\).


 {definition}[ {Bau2022Htype}]
An H-type foliation is said to be 
 {itemize}
      of  {Yang-Mills type}, if $  _{ {H}}^{  }T=0$;
     with horizontally parallel torsion, if $  _{ {H}}T=0$;
       with completely parallel torsion, if $  T=0$.  
 {itemize}	
 {definition}

 {remark}
	The Yang-Mills assumption plays an important role in the theory of generalized curvature dimension inequalities. 
 {remark}

 {proposition}
	On an H-type foliation, one has for every $X    {X}_{ {H}}, Z    {X}_{ {V}}$, 
	$$ -  _{ {V}}([X,J_Z X])=|X|^2Z. $$
	Thus, the horizontal distribution is bracket generating of step-two.
 {proposition}
 {proof}
	Note that 
	$$ -  _{ {V}}([X,J_Z X])=T(X, J_Z X) .$$
	By polarization, the H-type condition implies the Clifford relation
 {equation} {clif}
	J_ZJ_W+J_WJ_Z=-2  Z,W  {Id}_{  H}.
 {equation}
From this we see 
$$   -  _{ {V}}([X,J_{e_{  }} X]), e_{  }   =-   X,J_{e_{  }}J_{e_{  }}X   =   X,J_{e_{  }}J_{e_{  }}X   +2   _{    }|X|^2.$$
But 
$$   X,J_{e_{  }}J_{e_{  }}X   =-   J_{e_{   }}X,J_{e_{   }}X   =    X,J_{e_{  }}J_{e_{  }}X   ,$$
hence 
$$   -  _{ {V}}([X,J_{e_{  }} X]), e_{  }   =   _{    }|X|^2.$$
 {proof}

In fact, the proof states a slightly stronger pointwise fact: once you fix any nonzero horizontal vector \(X_p\),
\[
T_pM
=
  H_p+[X,  H]_p.
\]

 {theorem}[ {Bau2022Htype}]
	H-type foliations are Yang-Mills.
 {theorem}

 {Clifford representation}
The H-type condition endows the horizontal bundle with a natural
Clifford-module structure. Indeed,
we have seen from  {clif} 
the following Clifford relation
\[
    J_ZJ_W+J_WJ_Z
    =
    -2  Z,W 
     {Id}_{  H},
      Z,W   V.
\]
Consequently, at each \(p  M\), the map
\[
      V_p  {End}(  H_p),
     
    Z  J_Z,
\]
extends naturally to a representation
\[
    J: {Cl}(  V_p)
     
     {End}(  H_p)
\]
of the Clifford algebra of \(  V_p\). In particular,
\[
    J_1= {Id}_{  H_p},
     
    J_{Z  W}=J_ZJ_W,
\]
where \(Z  W\) denotes Clifford multiplication. Thus compositions
of the operators \(J_Z\) are themselves encoded by the Clifford
algebra of the vertical space.

This representation provides a useful description of the algebra
generated by the vertical directions. Let \(  a(p)\) denote
the Lie algebra of endomorphisms of \(  H_p\) generated by
\(\{J_Z:Z   V_p\}\), where the bracket is the commutator
\([A,B]=AB-BA\). As shown in
 {Bau2022Htype}, no higher-order commutators
are needed to generate \(  a(p)\): it is generated by the
operators
\[
    J_Z
      {and} 
    [J_Z,J_W].
\]
More precisely, either \(\{J_Z:Z   V_p\}\) is already closed
under commutators, or
\[
      a(p)
     
     {so}(k+1),
\]
where \(k=   V\).

The first possibility is particularly restrictive. If the family
\(\{J_Z\}\) is itself closed under commutators, then either \(k=1\),
in which case the resulting structure is of complex type, or \(k=3\),
in which case the operators \(J_Z\), together with the identity,
satisfy the quaternionic multiplication rules. In the latter case one
can choose a local orthonormal vertical frame
\(\{Z_1,Z_2,Z_3\}\) such that, up to orientation,
\[
    J_{Z_1}J_{Z_2}=J_{Z_3}, 
    J_{Z_2}J_{Z_3}=J_{Z_1}, 
    J_{Z_3}J_{Z_1}=J_{Z_2},
\]
and
\[
    J_{Z_ }^2=- {Id}_{  H}.
\]
This motivates the notion of an H-type foliation of
 {quaternionic type}; in particular, such a foliation necessarily
has vertical rank three. Important examples include \(3K\)-contact,
\(3\)-Sasakian, and quaternionic Heisenberg geometries.

If, in addition, the torsion is horizontally parallel,
\[
     _{  H}T=0,
\]
then the above algebraic type is independent of the point. Indeed,
parallel transport along horizontal curves intertwines the operators
\(J_Z\), while the H-type condition implies that \(  H\) is
bracket generating. Hence the Clifford-algebra structure at one point
determines the corresponding structure throughout the connected
manifold.

 {H-type groups}

H-type foliations may be viewed as a geometric generalization of the classical H-type groups introduced by Kaplan (cf.  {Kapl1980Htype} or  {Bau2022Htype}). 

Recall that an H-type group is a connected simply connected two-step nilpotent Lie group \(G\) whose Lie algebra admits an orthogonal decomposition
\[
      g=  h   z,
\]
where \(  z\) is the center of \(  g\), such that
\[
    [  h,  h]   z,
     
    [  g,  z]=0.
\]
For \(Z   z\), define \(J_Z:  h   h\) by
\[
      J_ZX,Y 
    =
      Z,[X,Y]  .
\]
The H-type condition is
\[
    J_Z^2=-|Z|^2 {Id}_{  h},
      Z   z.
\]
